entities.summary: Yang Feng was a bandit leader and military general who played a crucial role in the late Eastern Han dynasty of China. Born in the 1st century AD, Yang Feng rose to prominence as a leader of the Red Turban Rebellion, a peasant uprising that aimed to overthrow the corrupt and divided Han dynasty. Through his military campaigns, Yang Feng established a network of alliances and vassal states, stretching from modern-day Shandong Province in the north to Hainan Island in the south. His military prowess and strategic brilliance earned him the respect of his peers and the fear of his enemies. Yang Feng's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also played a key role in the development of the Five Dynasties period, which saw the collapse of the Tang dynasty and the rise of the Jin dynasty. As the Jin dynasty's founder, Yang Feng's name became synonymous with the dynasty's founding and his legacy continues to be celebrated in Chinese history and culture. He died on April 1, 197 AD, in a battle against the warlord Cao Cao. Yang Feng's life and legacy serve as a testament to the enduring power of military leadership and strategic brilliance in shaping the course of Chinese history.
